key_insight: AI agents could deepen societal inequality when people differ in access to them, how capable their agents are, and how many they can use. This paper develops a conceptual framework for understanding these risks and outlines a research agenda to address them.
problem_solved: Addresses the need to identify and study how unequal access to AI agents—and differences in their quality and number—could create or reinforce societal inequalities.
method: Develop a conceptual framework to identify potential sources of agentic inequality.
Examine disparities in access to AI agents, agent quality, and the number of agents available.
Propose a research agenda to better understand and address the resulting societal challenges.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the framework highlights why agent capability alone is not enough: who can access and deploy agents also matters. It encourages attention to distributional effects when developing and deploying agentic systems.
visual_elements: Three-axis diagram showing access, agent quality, and agent quantity as dimensions of inequality.
Side-by-side illustration of people supported by different numbers and capabilities of AI agents.
Conceptual flow diagram linking unequal agent resources to potential societal disparities.
Research roadmap connecting sources of inequality to open questions and possible responses.
paper_authors: Matthew Sharp, Omer Bilgin, Iason Gabriel, Lewis Hammond
